title: Contrastive Semi-Supervised Segmentation with Class-wise Patches and Silhouette-Adaptive Consistency
abstract: We present CSSL, a contrastive semi-supervised method for medical image segmentation. CSSL samples class-wise patches from labelled images and from confident pseudo-labels, separates their embeddings with a supervised contrastive loss with mixed hard negatives, and uses the Silhouette coefficient of the embedding clusters to set the strength of a feature-perturbation consistency loss. On MoNuSeg, patch embeddings are obtained by masked pooling of the encoder features of the unmasked image, nucleus rims form an additional contrastive class and a memory bank stores past embeddings; on CHAOS, patches are pixel-masked and no memory bank is used. The CSSL losses are added to a weak-to-strong pseudo-labelling recipe. We follow the protocols of published baselines: Self-Loop on MoNuSeg and DAFNet on CHAOS. On MoNuSeg with 50% labels, CSSL reaches 80.87 $\pm$ 0.17 nuclei F1 over three label splits, compared with 79.10 for Self-Loop and 78.73 for the same recipe without CSSL. On CHAOS T2 with 25% labels, CSSL reaches 89.01 Dice, compared with 82.0 for DAFNet and 88.94 for the recipe alone. Ablations show that the contrastive branch and, on MoNuSeg, the boundary class and feature-level pooling account for most of the improvement. Code: https://github.com/prinshul/CSSL
